column5: text
Imagine being swallowed by a whale.
One moment, you're swimming through the ocean.
The next, a gigantic mouth engulfs you.
Everything goes dark.
You crash through rushing water, surrounded by fish and enormous baleen plates.
Then the mouth closes.
And you realize...
You're trapped inside a living giant.
You try to find an opening.
But every direction looks the same.
Water slams against your body as the whale moves through the ocean.
You scream, but nobody can hear you.
You try to swim toward the light...
Only to be thrown backward by another powerful surge of water.
Then you realize something terrifying.
You don't know when the whale will open its mouth again.
Your chest tightens.
Your air supply is running low.
Every movement costs energy you can no longer afford to waste.
The whale dives deeper, and the sunlight disappears completely.
You feel the enormous animal moving around you.
Its muscles shift.
Its body vibrates with every movement.
You're not inside a cave.
You're inside a creature that doesn't even know you're there.
Then, suddenly, everything changes.
The whale accelerates toward the surface.
Light flashes through the water.
You fight your way toward the opening as the current drags you forward.
For one second, you can see the sky.
Then the whale opens its mouth.
Water erupts around you.
And you're thrown back into the ocean.
You surface, gasping for air.
Your body is exhausted.
Your equipment is damaged.
The whale disappears beneath the waves, leaving you alone in the open ocean.
You survived being trapped inside one of the largest animals on Earth.
But now you face a new problem.
You have no idea how far you are from shore.
And your remaining air won't last forever.
You look down into the dark water.
Something enormous moves beneath you.
For a moment, you freeze.
Then you realize the truth.
Being swallowed by a whale was never the only danger.
The ocean is enormous.
You're exhausted, stranded, and running out of air.
And this time...
There may be nobody coming to save you.
